depth.h2: What Elmhurst Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: The median home in Elmhurst was built in 1966. About 4 in 10 went up between 1940 and 1969, about 1 in 7 is older than that, and about 3 in 10 have been built since 1990. Here’s what that mix means for your plumbing.

tiles.title: Postwar Sewer Lines and Tree Roots
tiles.body: Sewer lines from the 1940s, 50s and 60s were usually clay. Decades of roots from mature parkway trees get in at the joints and slowly close the pipe. [Hydro jetting](/elmhurst/hydro-jetting) scours the roots and buildup off the pipe walls, and a [camera inspection](/elmhurst/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows whether the line needs a [repair](/elmhurst/sewer-repair).

tiles.title: April 2013: 7 Inches of Rain in Two Days
tiles.body: On April 17 and 18, 2013, Elmhurst got 7.26 inches of rain, and homes old and new across town had water damage. It wasn’t the first time: residents saw the same scenes in 2010, in the same neighborhoods. A [sump pump with a battery backup](/elmhurst/sump-pumps) and a [backflow valve](/elmhurst/flood-control-maintenance) are the best protection.

tiles.title: Hard Water and Water Heaters
tiles.body: Elmhurst’s Lake Michigan water comes through the DuPage Water Commission, and the city reports its hardness at about 8 grains per gallon. That’s enough to build scale in a tank water heater over the years. A yearly flush helps, and when a heater starts to rumble, leak or run out fast, we can [repair or replace it](/elmhurst/water-heater-repair).

tiles.title: Winter Freezes and Burst Pipes
tiles.body: Elmhurst winters bring long stretches below freezing. Pipes in exterior walls, crawl spaces and outdoor spigot lines freeze first, and a split pipe often starts leaking inside a wall once it thaws. We’re on call 24/7 for [burst pipe repair](/elmhurst/burst-pipe-repair).

items.q: How much does a plumber cost in Elmhurst?
items.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in. Give us a call and we’ll walk you through it.

items.q: What’s the difference between sewer rodding and hydro jetting?
items.preview: Rodding uses a cutting cable to open a path through a clog.
items.a: Rodding uses a cutting cable to open a path through a clog. Hydro jetting uses high-pressure water to clean the whole pipe wall, so roots, grease and scale come off instead of being punched through. For older clay lines where roots keep coming back, [hydro jetting](/elmhurst/hydro-jetting) usually lasts longer. We camera the line first to make sure it’s the right choice.

items.q: How often should I have my sewer line cleaned?
items.preview: If roots have blocked your line before, once a year is typical.
items.a: If roots have blocked your line before, once a year is typical. If you’ve never had a problem, a camera inspection every few years is a good way to catch roots early. We can set up [regular sewer maintenance](/elmhurst/sewer-maintenance) so you don’t have to remember.

items.preview: Yes. The city reports about 8 grains per gallon, which counts as hard water.
items.a: Yes. The city reports about 8 grains per gallon, which counts as hard water. It’s enough to build scale in water heaters and on fixtures over time. Flushing your water heater once a year helps it last longer.

items.q: How do I protect my basement from flooding?
items.preview: Start with a sump pump in good shape, a battery backup in case the power goes out and a backflow valve on your sewer line.
items.a: Start with a sump pump in good shape, a battery backup in case the power goes out and a backflow valve on your sewer line. For homes with repeat backups, an [overhead sewer system](/elmhurst/overhead-sewer-systems) lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen.
